Gilbert Villarreal | key_people = | industry = [[Automotive industry|Automotive]] | founded = {{start date and age|2012}} | products = [[VLF Destino]]
[[VLF Force 1 V10]] | website = {{URL|http://www.vlfautomotive.com/|vlfautomotive.com}} }} '''VLF Automotive''' was a small American-based automotive company formed in January 2016. It was founded as '''VL Automotive''' in 2012 by [[Bob Lutz (businessman)|Bob Lutz]] and Gilbert Villarreal, then renamed after [[Henrik Fisker]] joined the company. [[GreenTech Automotive]] merged with VL Automotive in 2014. GreenTech produced few cars, if any. It declared bankruptcy in February 2018. ==Company history== The company was founded by designer and entrepreneur [[Henrik Fisker]], ex-[[General Motors]] vice-chairman Bob Lutz and industrialist Gilbert Villarreal. The company's name is taken from the initials of their surnames.{{cite magazine|last=Lavrinc|first=Damon|title=Fisker Karma Gets a 638-HP Corvette Heart Transplant|url=https://www.wired.com/autopia/2013/01/vlp-destino/|magazine=Wired|access-date=May 25, 2013|date=January 14, 2013}} In 2013 they displayed the [[VLF Destino|Destino]], its first model, based on the [[Fisker Karma]], at the [[North American International Auto Show]] in Detroit. [[GreenTech Automotive]] merged with VL Automotive in 2014.{{cite web|title=GreenTech Scatters New Seeds|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/18/automobiles/greentech-scatters-new-seeds.html?_r=0|website=New York Times|access-date=28 May 2015|date=16 May 2014|first=Jim|last=Motavalli|url-access=limited}}{{cite web|title=Destino's VL Automotive merges with GreenTech Automotive|url=https://www.autoblog.com/2014/05/06/destinos-vl-automotive-merges-with-greentech-automotive/?guccounter=1|website=Autoblog|access-date=6 June 2015|date=6 May 2014|first=Sebastian|last=Blanco}}[https://www.autoblog.com/news/destinos-vl-automotive-merges-with-greentech-automotive "Destino's VL Automotive merges with GreenTech Automotive,"] Autoblog. GreenTech produced few cars, if any.[https://www.baconsrebellion.com/where-did-140-million-in-greentech-money-go/ "Where Did $140 Million in GreenTech Money Go?,"] ''Bacon's Rebellion''. It declared bankruptcy in February 2018.{{cite web|url=http://www.richmond.com/news/local/government-politics/greentech-the-electric-car-company-once-led-by-mcauliffe-files/article_bf83ede4-ae12-5561-ad3b-b0a29c2b0984.html |title=GreenTech files for bankruptcy |last=Oliver |first=Ned |publisher=Richmond Times-Dispatch |date=27 February 2018 |url-access=limited}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/greentech-automotive-files-for-bankruptcy-1519775795|title=GreenTech Automotive Files for Bankruptcy|last=Yerak|first=Becky|date=28 February 2018|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=2020-02-06|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}} As of May 2025, the company website is no longer operational. ==Products== ===VLF Destino=== {{see also|VLF Destino}} The [[VLF Destino]] four-door sedan was first shown in January 2013, heavily based on the [[Fisker Karma]], but fitted with a 6.2 L V8 gasoline engine rather than the electric power of the Karma. Sales of the Destino were scheduled to commence in the second half of 2015, with cars to be built in [[Auburn Hills]] in Michigan,{{cite web|last=Nunez|first=Alex|title=Destino: Bob Lutz's Corvette-powered Fisker Karma|url=http://www.roadandtrack.com/go/first-looks/destino-bob-lutz-corvette-powered-fisker-karma|work=Road & Track|access-date=May 25, 2013|date=January 14, 2013}} but the company only obtained 20 Fisker Karma "[[Glider (automobiles)|gliders]]" and reported 100 orders by May 2013.{{cite web|last=Smith|first=David|title=Fisker Woes Won't Dash Destino Plans|url=http://wardsauto.com/vehicles-amp-technology/fisker-woes-won-t-dash-destino-plans|work=Wards Auto|access-date=May 25, 2013|date=May 3, 2013}} At the January 2014 Detroit Autoshow, the company announced that production was delayed due to the ongoing restructuring of Fisker.{{cite web|title=Detroit reveal for VL Destino convertible|url=http://www.autocar.co.uk/car-news/detroit-motor-show/detroit-reveal-vl-destino-convertible|work=Autocar|access-date=January 19, 2014|date=January 14, 2014}} ===VLF Force 1=== {{main|VLF Force 1}} The company announced production of a limited edition 745 HP American sports car [[VLF Force 1|Force 1]] V10, limited to 50 by third quarter 2016. The car was a Coach Built [[Dodge Viper (VX I)|Dodge Viper]]. In 2016 they debuted the Force 1, a 745 hp American sports car at the [[North American International Auto Show]].{{citation needed|date=December 2024}} ===VLF Rocket V8=== In 2018, VLF partnered with [[Galpin Auto Sports]] to produce the Rocket V8, a coach built [[Ford Mustang (sixth generation)|Ford Mustang]] that was to be co built by both VLF and Galpin Auto Sports.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}} ===HUMVEE C-Series=== Beginning in 2017, VLF was contracting a version of the [[HMMWV]]/[[Hummer H1]] for the non-Americas market with limited run of 100 units per year via contract from [[AM General]]. Markets include China, Europe and the Middle East.{{Cite web |url=http://gmauthority.com/blog/2017/05/vlf-is-now-building-and-selling-the-hummer-h1-to-china/ |title=VLF is Now Building and Selling the Hummer H1 to China |date=9 May 2017 |access-date=2024-05-07}} AM General had announced offering the C-Series as a kit for sale in 2012, but cancelled the project.{{cite web |url=https://www.motortrend.com/news/diy-h1-am-general-announces-new-59995-civilian-humvee-c-series-kits-283673/ |title=AM General Announces New $59,995 Civilian Humvee C-Series Kits |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710181441/https://www.motortrend.com/news/diy-h1-am-general-announces-new-59995-civilian-humvee-c-series-kits-283673/ |archive-date=July 10, 2019 |url-status=live |access-date=2024-05-07}} ==See also== * [[Henrik Fisker]] * [[Bob Lutz (businessman)|Bob Lutz]] * [[Fisker Coachbuild]] (2005–2007) * [[Fisker Automotive]] (2007–2014) * [[VIA Motors]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{official website|http://www.vlfautomotive.com}} {{Automotive industry in the United States}} {{Henrik Fisker}} [[Category:Coachbuilders of the United States]] [[Category:Car manufacturers of the United States]] [[Category:Motor vehicle manufacturers based in Michigan]] [[Category:Henrik Fisker]] [[Category:Luxury motor vehicle manufacturers]] [[Category:American companies established in 2012]] [[Category:Vehicle manufacturing companies established in 2012]]
